In this Tuesday, June 18, 2019, photo, two boys jokingly take cover as small toy poops gush from a giant poop-shaped inflatable at the Unko Museum in Yokohama, south of Tokyo. In a country known for its cult of cute, even poop is not an exception. A pop-up exhibition at the Unko Museum in the port city of Yokohama is all about unko, a Japanese word for poop. The poop installations there get their cutest makeovers. They come in the shape of soft cream, or cupcake toppings. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong)

In 2008, when my family moved from Manhattan to Darien, CT, my wife and I wanted our two boys (aged 5 and 7 at the time) to continue their Mandarin instruction. Although my wife and I were conversant in Cantonese, we always pushed for Mandarin, as it?s become the dominant dialect in China. In addition, the public elementary schools my sons attended were excellent, but did not have much ethnic diversity. CLS has the ethnic diversity as well as the structure to teach oral and writing skills in the traditional or simplified method. 

My expectation was to have my sons be prepared to take the AP exams in high schools, if they wanted to go down that route. CLS has exceeded my expectations, and also helped my sons to create lifelong friends. CLS is not just a place to learn Mandarin and the Chinese culture- it?s a community!
— Steven C.

Pig Point Ranch; Bow or rifle. Cow Mountain area north of Clear Lake. Meet up at their ranch house early in the morning check your license and tag(s), sign the waiver and pay the fees and they take you to the mountain in a ATV. Plenty of boars but terrain is rough. One day hunt cost $500 (one pig) includes 1 on 1 guide and skinning and gutting the pig (add'l tip is up to you).
